text.p: The Malta Stock Exchange share index dropped 16.1 points to 991.42 in the once weekly trading session on Wednesday in quiet trade.
Market turnover on Wednesday reached just over 200,650 Maltese lira ($541,755) from the previous week's 714,250 Maltese lira. There were 60 deals, 36 in equities and 24 in fixed income securities.

Turnover in equities amounted to just over 66,300 Maltese lira, with 51,875 shares being transacted. Of these, 24,438 were Bank of Valletta shares transacted in 23 deals for an average 124 cents, unchanged from last week.
There were nine deals in Mid-Med Bank with 20,435 shares selling for an average 148 cents each, down one cent.
In Lombard Bank Malta, which was trading ex-dividend, 500 shares were sold for 145 cents, down from 153.3 cents when last traded two weeks ago.

A total of 4,000 Farsons ordinary shares sold for an average 51 cents per share, unchanged. In the 8.5 percent Farsons preference shares 1996/99, 502 shares were sold for an average price one lira, down five mils while in the six percent preference shares 100 shares were transacted in three deals at an average 10.57 lira, down one cent.
The government bond market saw trading in the nine issues for a turnover of 130,800 lira. Business was mainly in the seven percent MGS (2003 III) and the 7.5 percent MGS 2011.
In corporate bonds, there were three deals in Mid-Med Bank 7.25 percent unsecured loan stock 2005 amounting to 2,476.50 lira.
